head: 6d350f79dacd41cecb0c0e80d2c62ffb8b723dd8
review_scope: Read-only source review of the exact five local SQL diffs and directly adjacent account/ordinal/allocation consumers; no active edits, child agents, Native execution or independent audit claim.
expected: Only absent optional account snapshots become SQL NULL; selected credit/cash object snapshots retain their complete contents and current-master verification.
Reject JSON null/scalar/array snapshots in private rows after normalization; an object-only CHECK must not be mistaken for complete source/authority proof.
One component row per internally generated component identity/ordinal, preserving numeric ordinal order and all constituent parts/amounts.
The allocation residual limit remains original allocation quantity minus prior POSTED returns for that exact allocation, retaining the Native allocation refusal code.

findings.assessment: CLEAR in the actual sealed-builder path
findings.observed: seal_return_settlement normalizes b.credit_account_snapshot and b.cash_account_snapshot using nullif(value, JSON null) both in initial_return_work INSERT and return_command_scope UPDATE. Other JSON values are unchanged. New CHECKs admit SQL NULL or object only; JSON null has jsonb_typeof=null-text and fails, as do arrays/scalars.
findings.cross_stage_proof: build_initial_return_for_draft_v1 calls strict credit_account_facts_v1/cash_account_facts_v1 for every selected account before constructing the quote; missing required choices add readiness issues, and sealing requires READY plus exact quote/authority binding. Existing assertions recheck every present credit account master and cash facts. Recognition requires nonnull credit snapshot; REFUND operations additionally require a nonnull object cash snapshot and verify current snapshot equality. No permission, date, account predicate or refund check was removed.
findings.boundary: The object CHECK alone allows {} and SQL NULL and does not prove selected-account presence. Safety here depends on the existing private builder/READY/seal and later recognition/refund verifiers, which remain intact. No new public snapshot input or scope-writing capability is introduced.

findings.observed: Only ORDER BY changes from (z->>component_ordinal)::integer to (z->component_ordinal)::integer, matching the JSONB expression already present in GROUP BY. Group keys, SELECT payload and all INSERT values are unchanged.
findings.cross_stage_proof: parts is built internally with component_ordinal=n, where n is integer and increments once per kernel component. component UUID is generated once before its part loop; every part of that component carries the same UUID, component JSON and numeric ordinal. GROUP BY still emits one row for that component and numeric JSONB-to-integer ordering places 2 before 10. The parts aggregation/hash still independently sorts numeric component ordinal and part ordinal. All part rows are inserted afterward unchanged.
findings.boundary: Casting JSONB string ordinals would fail rather than silently use lexical ordering; caller-supplied parts are not accepted by this function.

findings.observed: The exact per-allocation overflow predicate was extracted from the existing OR guard and now raises AH_RETURN_EXCEEDS_ORIGINAL_ALLOCATION before the unchanged owned<0 / aggregate sold-returned HPP guard. No quantity term or prior POSTED-row filter was removed.
findings.native_source_reference: supabase/migrations/20260916070451_erp_v2_6_20ah_cp6_return_allocation_eligibility.sql:281-289 uses prior POSTED returns for the selected allocation plus current-document allocation quantity compared against original allocation quantity.
findings.cross_stage_proof: The projection first proves allocation belongs to the sale. Allocation UUID uniquely identifies its source; the actual owning own-return exclusion is DRAFT, so status POSTED excludes it automatically. Existing validate_return rejects duplicate allocation IDs in one request, making the per-item proposed quantity equal the current-document quantity for that allocation. Other allocation IDs and reversed prior returns do not consume this allocation residual. The residual and aggregate invalid-source cases all still refuse; only precedence/error code for overflow changes intentionally.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: Normalize to SQL NULL, pass optional CHECK, skip only the absent cash recheck; preserve and recheck the selected credit object.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.input: REFUND with selected valid cash object
counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: Object survives NULLIF byte-for-byte as JSONB, stays nonnull, reaches both existing work/source and refund cash proof checks.
Builder readiness issue / strict facts refusal prevents seal; recognition/refund nonnull guards remain additional refusal. The new nullable object CHECK alone is not relied upon for this guarantee.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.input: JSON null / array / scalar inserted directly as a snapshot
counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: CHECK rejects each non-object, non-SQL-NULL value; normalizing a scalar/array does not convert it to NULL.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.input: Several parts for component ordinals 2 and 10
counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: Exactly one grouped component row for each generated component; numeric order 2 then 10; all parts and sums retained.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: AH_RETURN_EXCEEDS_ORIGINAL_ALLOCATION before extra aggregate HPP target check; no posting/closure bypass.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.input: Original allocation qty=2, prior POSTED return qty=1, new qty=1
counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: Residual guard allows equality; all existing source/HPP/financial checks still apply.

counterexample_controls_considered_not_e.expected: Existing CP7_SALES_RETURN_DUPLICATE_ALLOCATION refusal before projection; normalization/grouping does not weaken it.
